rendererLocal.lifecycle: Rust owns the fallback dispatch, state transition, response projection, and presentation. Reserved private commands always remain local; for every other name an authoritative runtime catalog collision wins first.

runtimeCatalog.lifecycle: TypeScript advertises only an enabled renderer-neutral implementation; Rust dispatches only an advertised token and otherwise fails closed.

failClosedGroups.reason: The reference command depends on a desktop/JSX workspace panel or OS integration that has no truthful pure-TUI lifecycle.
The command requires a mobile, desktop, office, daemon, or remote-control authority outside the pure TUI process.
The reference command owns a session/history mutation or picker whose complete transactional lifecycle has not been ported to the native renderer.
The command is an interactive permissions, planning, task, hook, or sandbox management surface and must not be approximated by a backend text send.
The command requires an authenticated service manager, updater, or account-specific status surface that is not available through the direct runtime contract.
The command depends on an interactive mode/review UI whose complete state and cancellation semantics have not been ported.

statusDefinitions.verified: A token-complete assertion or an exact command-specific lifecycle test exists and is pinned by evidence below.
statusDefinitions.shared_path_only: The common transport/projection path is verified, but every command-specific outcome branch is not independently exercised.
statusDefinitions.not_applicable: The lifecycle phase cannot occur for this profile by design; the note states the closed boundary.
statusDefinitions.unverified: No machine-verifiable evidence currently closes this phase; the note is an actionable audit gap.

scope.ownerBoundary: Lifecycle statuses cover the direct TUI owner boundary: token discovery, exact dispatch, correlated completion truth, renderer input, and TUI transcript recovery.
scope.externalAuthorityBoundary: Network services, operating-system integrations, and command-specific business mutations behind an admitted handler are separate authorities; this audit neither invokes them nor labels their internal effects as renderer success.
scope.hermeticRuntimeSeam: Production smoke loads every real command and executes each actual handler with mocks only at external authority seams. The separate runtime matrix verifies the shared slash-dispatch, terminal projection, renderer-input, and physical transcript machinery without pretending its injected handler is command-specific business evidence.

ownershipPrecedence.unknownTokenPolicy: Preserve the existing backend slash resolver; the renderer must not invent either success or failure.

discovery.knownUnavailableWhenUnadvertised: Runtime-catalog and fail-closed profile tokens are omitted from completion/help when absent and are consumed by the renderer without backend send. A valid independently advertised collision is catalog-owned instead.
